market_context: US/Canada audience; deciding which pregnancy details to share.
title: How to decide which pregnancy details you want to share and which you do not

seo.title: How to decide which pregnancy details to share or keep private
seo.meta_description: Create layers of privacy for appointments, dates, photos, and plans without feeling that every piece of pregnancy information needs the same rule.
seo.search_intent: Help pregnant women decide which pregnancy information to share and with whom.

excerpt: You do not have to choose between telling everyone everything and saying nothing. Different information can have different circles of access.
content_html:
Once people know you are pregnant, questions can multiply: due date, appointments, names, sex, birth plans, hospital, pictures, results, or visitor plans. It can feel as though sharing the headline opened access to every detail underneath it.

There is no single package called “pregnancy information.” You can create layers of access.

Sort information by how it feels to share

Some details may be fun to talk about, some may belong with two trusted people, and some may feel private until after the baby arrives. You do not need to justify why a due month feels public while an appointment feels personal.

Consider each person's ability to keep information contained

Emotional closeness is not always the same as discretion. If someone routinely forwards pictures or spreads updates, decide whether you want them to receive a detail before it is public.

Revisit privacy as pregnancy changes

Something you did not want to share early may stop feeling sensitive later, and information that once felt neutral may become more private. Your rules can evolve without making the earlier boundary unreasonable.

Use answers that do not open a negotiation

“We're not sharing that yet,” “we're keeping that part to ourselves,” or “we'll let you know when we're ready” can close a question without inventing an excuse.

Privacy does not mean rejecting closeness. Pregnancy touches your body, family, health, and future, which is exactly why it can help to decide deliberately what remains yours or belongs only to your closest circle.

faq.question: Do I have to give the same information to every relative?
faq.answer: No. Different people can have different levels of access depending on the information and your comfort.

faq.question: Can I change my mind and share something later?
faq.answer: Yes. Boundaries can change as pregnancy and your comfort change.

faq.question: What can I say when someone asks for a detail I do not want to share?
faq.answer: A short line such as “we're not sharing that yet” is enough.
